summary: Elena Beccarini-Crescenzi was an Indologist who studied at the University of Florence until 1915 under Paolo Emilio Pavolini.
Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a scholar of Tibetology. She studied East Asian history at the Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech until 1971 and became an associate professor there in 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey, attested in 1998.

Elena Mucciarelli works in Indology and religious studies. She completed a PhD in Indology at the University of Tübingen (c. 2006–2010), worked there (2016–2017), at Hebrew University (2017–2020), and became an assistant professor at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate under Charles Malamoud (c. 1978–1980) and habilitated at Hamburg (1997). He held the chair of Indology at the University of Leipzig from 2004 to 2021.

Elijah George Halhed Impey (1818–1868) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Bombay Medical Service (1840), as Surgeon-Major in the Bombay Army (c. 1840–1864), and as Postmaster-General of the Bombay Presidency (1856–1868).

Elijah Sacvan Ary is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and earned a PhD at Harvard University (c. 1999–2007) under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Elimar Benda (1890–1976) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who earned a Dr.iur. at the University of Jena in 1913. He served as a librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1921–1922), Freiburg (1926–1936), and Heidelberg (1936–1940).

Elimar Max Grube (1851–1891) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Rudolf von Roth, completing his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber in 1874–1875.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1960. He taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).

Elisa Freschi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella (c. 2003–2006). She worked at Sapienza University, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and became Associate Professor of South Asian Philosophy at Toronto around 2020.
Elisa Ganser is an Indologist. She worked as an SNF project collaborator at the University of Zurich in 2018 and is attested as a lecturer at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Elisabeth Kreyenborg was an Indologist who studied under Richard Schmidt and earned a PhD from the University of Münster by 1930. She later served as a librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft from 1943 to 1950.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees at Würzburg and Münster. She taught at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and was appointed Krister Stendahl Research Professor of Divinity at Harvard in 1988.
Eliz Hale is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD in Biomedical Engineering at UC Davis in 2023 and is attested as a graduate student at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

Eliza Marian Butler (1885–1959) studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (c. 1907–1911). She held posts at Owens College (c. 1929–1936), the University of Manchester (1936), and the University of Cambridge (c. 1936–1951).

Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University (2009–2016) under James L. Fitzgerald and became an assistant professor at Florida State University in 2018.

Elizabeth Colton Spooner (1851–1927) was an Indologist. She studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman and pursued studies at Harvard University, Radcliffe College, Yale University, and the American Institute of Sacred Literature.
Elizabeth De Michelis works in religious studies and Indology. She completed a master's at SOAS and a PhD at the University of Cambridge (c. 1996–2001), where she served as director in 2000.
Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Harunaga Isaacson and completed her PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 1999.
